hyps.why: Edge 4 reads node 1, which is fed only by edge 0, so a conv there is dead weight when edge 0 is none.
Edge 2 also reads node 1, so it contributes nothing when edge 0 removes node 1's input.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 is reachable only through the 0->1->2 path, so a conv on edge 5 gains less.
Removing edge 4 costs nothing when it is already disconnected, but it removes useful capacity otherwise.
Edge 2 is already dead when edge 0 is none, so deleting it is harmless compared with usually losing a useful path.
Edge 5 is much less useful when edge 1 is none, so removing it hurts less.
Adding a direct skip where there was no edge gives a large gain, whereas replacing a conv with a skip loses accuracy.
Replacing none with a conv on the direct edge adds a whole path, which helps more than upgrading an existing skip or pool.
Reconnecting node 1 through a conv enables several downstream paths, so the gain is larger than when swapping one existing op for another.
Edge 1 only matters through edge 5 to reach the output, so a conv on it is worth less when edge 5 is none.
